title: Zechariah Chapter 8 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Zechariah chapter 8 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Zechariah Chapter 8 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Zechariah Chapter 8.

questions.question: In Zechariah 8, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The word of the LORD of hosts came to me
I will save my people from the east country
There shall yet old men and old women dwell in the streets
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD of hosts came to me
questions.explanation: This is the first statement in the chapter, found in Zechariah 8:1.

questions.question: What did the LORD say He was jealous for in Zechariah 8?
questions.correctAnswer: Zion
questions.explanation: The LORD states in Zechariah 8:2 that He was jealous for Zion.

questions.question: What will Jerusalem be called according to Zechariah 8?
questions.correctAnswer: A city of truth
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:3 declares that Jerusalem shall be called a city of truth.

questions.question: Who will dwell in the streets of Jerusalem according to Zechariah 8?
questions.correctAnswer: Old men and old women
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:4 states that old men and old women shall dwell in the streets of Jerusalem.

questions.question: What will fill the streets of the city according to Zechariah 8?
questions.correctAnswer: Boys and girls
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:5 mentions that the streets shall be full of boys and girls playing.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about marvelous things in the eyes of the remnant?
options: Should it also be marvelous in mine eyes?
questions.correctAnswer: Should it also be marvelous in mine eyes?
questions.explanation: In Zechariah 8:6, the LORD questions if it should be marvelous in His eyes as well.

questions.question: From where will the LORD save His people according to Zechariah 8?
options: From the east country and the west country
questions.correctAnswer: From the east country and the west country
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:7 states that the LORD will save His people from the east and west countries.

questions.question: What will the people do in the midst of Jerusalem according to Zechariah 8?
options: They will fight for their land
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be my people
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:8 specifies that they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem and be the LORD's people.

questions.question: What does the LORD declare about His relationship with the people?
options: He will be their God in truth and in righteousness
He will only be their God in war
He will not dwell among them
questions.correctAnswer: He will be their God in truth and in righteousness
questions.explanation: According to Zechariah 8:8, the LORD promises to be their God in truth and righteousness.

questions.question: The LORD expresses great jealousy for which location?
questions.correctAnswer: Zion
questions.explanation: This is stated directly in Zechariah 8:2 where the LORD mentions His jealousy for Zion.

questions.question: What will the old men and old women carry in the streets of Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: A staff
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:4 mentions that every man will have his staff in his hand for very age.

questions.question: The streets of the city will be full of boys and girls playing. Is this statement true?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is confirmed in Zechariah 8:5 which states that boys and girls will be playing in the streets.

questions.question: The LORD indicates He will not return to Zion. Is this statement true?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In Zechariah 8:3, the LORD states, 'I am returned unto Zion,' indicating His return.

questions.question: The LORD says He will gather His people only from the north. Is this statement true?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:7 specifically states He will save His people from both the east and west countries, not just the north.

questions.question: According to the text, Jerusalem will be a city of lies. Is this statement true?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:3 states that Jerusalem shall be called a city of truth, not lies.

medium.title: Zechariah Chapter 8 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Zechariah Chapter 8 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does the LORD of hosts instruct the people to do in Zechariah 8:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Let your hands be strong
questions.explanation: This is directly stated in Zechariah 8:9, where the LORD encourages the people to be strong as they hear the words of the prophets.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 8:10 indicate will occur if there is peace among the people?
options: There will be no hire for man
The heavens will not give dew
Men will be set against one another
questions.correctAnswer: The seed shall be prosperous
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:12 promises that if the people obey and have peace, the seed will be prosperous, indicating blessings in their endeavors.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He will not do to the residue of the people in Zechariah 8:11?
options: Punish them as in the former days
questions.correctAnswer: Punish them as in the former days
questions.explanation: In Zechariah 8:11, the LORD explicitly states that He will not treat the residue of the people as He did in the past.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 8:13, what transformation will occur for the house of Judah and Israel?
options: They will become a curse among the heathen
They will be saved and become a blessing
questions.correctAnswer: They will be saved and become a blessing
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:13 indicates that despite their previous status as a curse, they will be saved and turned into a blessing.

questions.question: What is promised in Zechariah 8:14 regarding the LORD's thoughts towards Jerusalem?
options: He will do well unto Jerusalem
He will bring affliction upon them
questions.correctAnswer: He will do well unto Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:15 reveals that the LORD intends to do well unto Jerusalem and the house of Judah, contrasting with His previous thoughts of punishment.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 8:16 say the people should do to maintain peace?
options: Speak the truth to their neighbors
questions.correctAnswer: Speak the truth to their neighbors
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:16 outlines that speaking the truth and executing judgment of truth and peace will foster a peaceful community.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 8:2 describe the LORD's feelings towards Zion?
questions.correctAnswer: With great jealousy and fury
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:2 details the LORD's intense jealousy and fury for Zion, indicating His deep concern for His people.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 8:3 promise about Jerusalem?
options: It will be a city of truth
It will be filled with enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It will be a city of truth
questions.explanation: In Zechariah 8:3, the LORD promises that Jerusalem will be called the city of truth, signifying a restoration of integrity.

questions.question: What demographic does Zechariah 8:4 mention will dwell in the streets of Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Old men and old women
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:4 mentions that old men and women will dwell in the streets, symbolizing peace and stability in the city.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 8:5 portray about the children in Jerusalem?
options: They will be playing in the streets
They will be sad and lonely
questions.correctAnswer: They will be playing in the streets
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:5 illustrates a joyful scene where boys and girls are playing in the streets, a sign of safety and happiness.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 8:6, how should the remnant view the promises of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: As marvellous
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:6 suggests that the LORD's promises should be seen as marvellous, emphasizing the greatness of His plans for them.

questions.question: What will the LORD do for His people according to Zechariah 8:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Bring them back from captivity
questions.explanation: In Zechariah 8:7, the LORD promises to save His people from the east and west, indicating His intention to restore them.

questions.question: Will the remnant be a curse among the heathen according to Zechariah 8:13?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:13 states that they will be saved and become a blessing, reversing their previous status as a curse.

questions.question: Did the LORD repent of His thoughts towards punishing the people according to Zechariah 8:14?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:14 indicates that the LORD did not repent of His thoughts to punish them in the past, showing the seriousness of their actions.

questions.question: Is Zechariah 8:15 a call to fear according to the LORD's promise?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:15 encourages the people not to fear, emphasizing hope and reassurance in the LORD's plans.

hard.title: Zechariah Chapter 8 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Zechariah Chapter 8.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 8:17, which of the following does the LORD explicitly state He hates?
options: Imagining evil in your hearts against your neighbour
questions.correctAnswer: Imagining evil in your hearts against your neighbour
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:17 states, 'And let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his neighbour; and love no false oath: for all these are things that I hate, saith the LORD.' Therefore, imagining evil and loving false oaths are explicitly hated by the LORD.

questions.question: Which fasts are transformed into joy and gladness for the house of Judah according to Zechariah 8?
options: The fast of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months
The fast of the first, second, third, and sixth months
Only the fast of the tenth month
The fast of the sixth and ninth months
questions.correctAnswer: The fast of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:19 specifies that the fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months shall be transformed into joy and gladness for the house of Judah.

questions.question: What is the primary reason given in Zechariah 8:19 for the change of fasts into joyful feasts?
options: Therefore love the truth and peace
questions.correctAnswer: Therefore love the truth and peace
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:19 concludes with 'therefore love the truth and peace,' indicating that loving truth and peace is the reason and result associated with the transformation of fasts into joyful feasts.

questions.question: In Zechariah 8:21, what do the inhabitants of one city say to those of another city?
options: "Let us go speedily to pray before the LORD, and to seek the LORD of hosts: I will go also."
"Let us build walls and protect our cities."
"Let us prepare sacrifices for the LORD."
questions.correctAnswer: "Let us go speedily to pray before the LORD, and to seek the LORD of hosts: I will go also."
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:21 records the invitation among inhabitants: 'Let us go speedily to pray before the LORD, and to seek the LORD of hosts: I will go also.'

questions.question: According to Zechariah 8:23, how many men from different languages will take hold of the skirt of a Jew?
questions.correctAnswer: Ten men
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:23 states, 'ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew.'

questions.question: What is the reason given in Zechariah 8:23 for the ten men from different nations to follow the Jew?
options: "For we have heard that God is with you."
questions.correctAnswer: "For we have heard that God is with you."
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:23 explains the motivation: 'We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'shalom' (שָׁלוֹם) as implied in Zechariah 8:19 primarily mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Peace and completeness
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'shalom' used in the context of Zechariah 8:19 means 'peace and completeness,' representing well-being and harmony.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Zechariah 8:23 when describing ten men from different languages holding the skirt of a Jew to go with them?
questions.correctAnswer: Typology
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:23 uses typology by prefiguring the inclusion of Gentiles with Jews, foreshadowing the New Testament inclusion of the Gentiles in God's people.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of many nations seeking the LORD as in Zechariah 8:22?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 2:2
questions.explanation: Isaiah 2:2 states that many nations shall come to the mountain of the LORD, echoing Zechariah 8:22's theme of many nations seeking the LORD in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the prophecy of Gentiles joining with Jews as in Zechariah 8:23?
questions.explanation: Acts 10:34-35 shows Peter declaring that God shows no partiality and accepts Gentiles who fear Him, fulfilling the prophecy in Zechariah 8:23 about nations joining with Jews.

questions.question: What immediately precedes Zechariah 8:17 in the chapter?
options: Execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates
I will bring them, and they shall dwell in Jerusalem
The fast of the fourth month
Old men and old women shall dwell in the streets
questions.correctAnswer: Execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:16 says, 'These are the things that ye shall do; Speak ye every man the truth to his neighbour; execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates,' which immediately precedes verse 17.

questions.question: In the context of Zechariah 8, what is the significance of 'the house of Judah' as mentioned in verses 19 and 15?
options: It represents the restored community of God's covenant people
It refers to a literal physical house in Jerusalem
It indicates the royal palace of the king
It symbolizes the enemies of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It represents the restored community of God's covenant people
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:15 and 19 use 'house of Judah' to symbolize the restored covenant community after exile, emphasizing God's blessing and renewed relationship.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 8:12 use agricultural imagery to represent God's blessing on His people?
options: Seed shall be prosperous, vine give fruit, ground give increase, heavens give dew
Fields shall be barren and vineyards dry
Trees shall be cut down and fields burned
Rivers shall overflow and flood the land
questions.correctAnswer: Seed shall be prosperous, vine give fruit, ground give increase, heavens give dew
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:12 uses agricultural blessings to symbolize prosperity and divine favor upon the remnant of His people.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 8:17 commands the people to love false oaths as a sign of faithfulness.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:17 explicitly says, 'love no false oath: for all these are things that I hate,' showing that false oaths are disliked by the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 8 prophesies that many people and strong nations shall come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:22 states, 'many people and strong nations shall come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem,' affirming this prophecy.

theological.title: Zechariah Chapter 8 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Zechariah Chapter 8 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Zechariah 8:3 teach about God's presence and covenant?
options: God is permanently absent from His people until the new heavens and new earth
God returns and dwells in the midst of Jerusalem as a sign of restored covenant fellowship
God's presence is conditional on Israel's perfect obedience
God only dwells spiritually with the Gentiles, not with Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: God returns and dwells in the midst of Jerusalem as a sign of restored covenant fellowship
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:3 states that God has returned unto Zion and will dwell in Jerusalem, indicating His renewed covenant presence with His people.

questions.question: What doctrine of God's justice and mercy is taught in Zechariah 8:14?
options: God repents after punishing Israel because He changes His mind
God is unchanging and does not repent, showing His steadfast justice
God initially intended punishment but chose mercy without regret
God's wrath is arbitrary and changes frequently
questions.correctAnswer: God initially intended punishment but chose mercy without regret
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:14 reveals that though God thought to punish Israel, He did not repent, showing a settled divine decision rooted in justice and mercy.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the ethical life of God's people is emphasized in Zechariah 8:16?
options: Believers are excused from speaking truth to maintain peace
God commands His people to speak truth and execute justice and peace in their communities
Ethical conduct is irrelevant to covenant faithfulness
Only priests are responsible for justice, not the people
questions.correctAnswer: God commands His people to speak truth and execute justice and peace in their communities
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:16 instructs God's people to speak truth to neighbors and uphold righteous judgment and peace, highlighting sanctification in community life.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Zechariah 8:2 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Jealousy
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:2 expresses God’s great jealousy for Zion, emphasizing His zeal for His covenant people.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly highlighted in Zechariah 8:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:12 shows God’s providence in causing the seed, vine, ground, and heavens to prosper for His people.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 8:7-8 connect to the broader biblical theme of the inclusion of the Gentiles?
options: It predicts Israel's final exile without restoration
It anticipates the gathering of God's people from all nations to dwell in Jerusalem
It limits God's salvation to the tribe of Judah only
It suggests that only the eastern nations will be saved
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the gathering of God's people from all nations to dwell in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:7-8 foretells God saving His people from east and west to dwell in Jerusalem, connecting with the biblical theme of the nations joining God's covenant people.

questions.question: In what way does Zechariah 8:23 anticipate the mission of the church in the New Testament?
options: It predicts the rejection of Jewish leadership by all nations
It shows Gentiles seeking to join themselves to God's people, foreshadowing the inclusion of the nations
It denies any future role for Gentiles in worship
It limits God's people to ethnic Israel exclusively
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Gentiles seeking to join themselves to God's people, foreshadowing the inclusion of the nations
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:23 depicts ten men from different languages clinging to a Jew to seek God, anticipating the Gentile mission of the New Testament church.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Zechariah 8:11 and 8:13 teach about God's covenant faithfulness and transformation of Israel's status?
options: God will reject Israel forever due to their sin
God will restore Israel from being a curse to becoming a blessing, demonstrating covenant faithfulness
Israel's curse is permanent and cannot be reversed
God's promises depend on Israel's perfect works
questions.correctAnswer: God will restore Israel from being a curse to becoming a blessing, demonstrating covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:11 and 8:13 together affirm that God will no longer treat Israel as in former days but will save them from curse to blessing, showing His steadfast covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What combined teaching about social ethics and divine hatred of injustice emerges from Zechariah 8:16 and 8:17?
options: God tolerates falsehood and evil in society
God commands truthfulness, just judgment, and condemns evil imaginations and false oaths
Ethical behavior is optional for covenant people
Peace is preferable even if it requires injustice
questions.correctAnswer: God commands truthfulness, just judgment, and condemns evil imaginations and false oaths
questions.explanation: Verses 16 and 17 together demand truthful speech, just judgment, and forbid evil intentions and false oaths, reflecting God's hatred for injustice.

questions.question: What doctrine about encouragement and divine strength is taught in Zechariah 8:9 and 8:15?
options: God commands passivity in face of hardship
God strengthens His people to rebuild and fear not, promising His favor
Human effort is irrelevant to divine work
Fear is necessary to motivate obedience
questions.correctAnswer: God strengthens His people to rebuild and fear not, promising His favor
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:9 and 8:15 both encourage strength and fearlessness, showing God’s empowering presence in restoration work.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the promises of restoration in Zechariah 8:10-13 are overly optimistic and ignore Israel's persistent sin. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God will restore Israel despite past afflictions and sin, showing His covenant grace
God will restore only if Israel is sinless
The passage ignores Israel's sin and focuses only on blessings
Restoration is purely symbolic with no real hope
questions.correctAnswer: God will restore Israel despite past afflictions and sin, showing His covenant grace
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:10-13 acknowledges past affliction and strife but promises prosperity and blessing for the remnant, demonstrating God’s grace beyond Israel’s sinfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine about the transformation of mourning into joy is taught in Zechariah 8:19?
options: Fasting remains a sign of sorrow without hope
God will turn days of fasting into joy and gladness for Judah
Joy is unrelated to covenant observance
questions.correctAnswer: God will turn days of fasting into joy and gladness for Judah
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:19 states that the traditional fasts will become times of joy and cheerful feasts, indicating God's restorative blessing.

questions.question: What combined theological insight about God's future gathering of peoples is found in Zechariah 8:20 and 8:22?
options: Only Israel will worship God in the last days
Many peoples and strong nations will seek the LORD in Jerusalem, showing universal worship
Foreign nations will abandon their gods but not worship Israel's God
Worship will be decentralized without any focus on Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Many peoples and strong nations will seek the LORD in Jerusalem, showing universal worship
questions.explanation: Verses 20 and 22 affirm that inhabitants of many cities and nations will come to Jerusalem to seek and pray before the LORD, expressing universal worship.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding the nature of God's jealousy is taught in Zechariah 8:2?
options: God’s jealousy is sinful human envy
God’s jealousy is a holy zeal for His covenant people’s exclusive devotion
God is indifferent to Israel’s loyalty
God’s jealousy leads Him to abandon His people
questions.correctAnswer: God’s jealousy is a holy zeal for His covenant people’s exclusive devotion
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:2 describes God’s jealousy for Zion with great jealousy and fury, indicating His holy zeal to protect covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine about peace and social harmony is taught in Zechariah 8:10?
options: Peace was absent because of affliction and division among people
Peace was abundant and unchallenged in former days
God ignores social strife among His people
questions.correctAnswer: Peace was absent because of affliction and division among people
questions.explanation: Zechariah 8:10 explains that previously there was no hire or peace because God set men against their neighbors, showing the reality of social brokenness due to sin and affliction.
